clue.text: Hold-up that's a blow to the church

parts.note: to hit is to strike, so a blow is a hit
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A setback described as a blow struck against the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a snag or delay that holds things up.

clue.text: Soundly disapproved Farrar's boy's fits

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so the phrase is spoken aloud

parts.note: hissed means disapproved noisily; Eric is the boy in Dean Farrar's Victorian school story Eric, or Little by Little

explanation.surface: A Victorian schoolboy's tantrums met with firm disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly', but signals the homophone: HISSED ERIC'S said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysterics are uncontrolled fits of emotion, laughing or crying.

clue.text: Emperor bird 'seen' over America

indicators.note: seen over in a down clue means the bird sits above the country

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: An emperor bird spotted flying over America.
explanation.walkthrough: Emperor penguin is the false path; the emperor is the Roman Titus.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was a Roman emperor, son of Vespasian.

clue.text: What do we get? Her years of sex-appeal ?

parts.note: taken as written
IT is old slang for sex appeal
an age is a long period of years

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what is left when her alluring years have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; the pieces run HER, IT, AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inheritance is what we receive from those before us, our heritage.

clue.text: Fungi rather than dandelion-clocks

definitions.meaning: round fungi that burst to release spores in a puff
the fluffy seed heads of dandelions, blown by children to tell the time

explanation.surface: A preference for mushrooms over the fluffy seed heads of dandelions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rather than' is a link: both the spore-puffing fungi and the round fluffy seed heads can be called by the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are soft round bodies that release a cloud of spores or seeds when disturbed.

clue.text: Pinch one who's over-conceited

explanation.definitionFit: To prig is archaic slang for to steal; a prig is a self-righteous, priggish person.

clue.text: Pubs for squatters ?

parts.note: pubs not tied to a brewery, read as dwellings anyone may occupy at no cost

explanation.surface: Bars that cater to people occupying empty buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub not tied to one brewery is a free house; squatters live in houses free of rent.

clue.text: Darwin's hound

definitions.meaning: The ship that carried Charles Darwin on his voyage

explanation.definitionFit: Darwin sailed aboard HMS Beagle; a beagle is also a small hunting dog.

clue.text: He makes free orbit, real crazy …

indicators.note: crazy suggests these letters are thrown into wild disorder

explanation.surface: Someone sets things loose with a bizarre circuit through space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges ORBIT REAL. The ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberator sets people free from oppression.

clue.text: … this Bolivar

parts.note: follows on from the previous clue: the first name of the South American liberator Bolivar

explanation.definitionFit: Simon Bolivar, the Venezuelan leader, was called El Libertador for freeing much of South America.

clue.text: Heavenly body in the East looks gloomy

parts.note: Saturn is a planet, a heavenly body
taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A planet rising in the eastern sky has a sombre air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks' is a link word here; the definition is the adjective 'gloomy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a dark, morose temperament, once blamed on the planet's astrological influence.

clue.text: Book Albert, worthless tramp

parts.note: Al is a short form of the name Albert
a bum is a vagrant or good-for-nothing

explanation.surface: Someone books a down-and-out man named Albert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb (to arrest or reserve) but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a book of blank pages for stamps or photographs.

clue.text: Imitation of a German

parts.note: read as a word for a substitute or fake that comes from the German language

explanation.surface: Someone does an impression of a German person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is borrowed from German, where it means substitute, and in English means a poor imitation.

clue.text: Issue that ought to be raised

definitions.text: Issue that ought to be raised

parts.words: Issue that ought to be raised
parts.note: reads like a matter for debate, but issue means offspring and raised means brought up

explanation.surface: A topic that deserves to be brought up for discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is legal language for offspring, and young offspring are reared by their parents.

clue.text: A literal definition of X is in order

definitions.text: A literal definition of X is in order

parts.words: A literal definition of X is in order
parts.note: literal means about letters: X comes third from last in the alphabet's order

explanation.surface: A precise explanation of some unknown is called for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in order' sounds like 'is appropriate' but means in alphabetical order; X is followed by Y and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Antepenult means the one before the next-to-last, as X precedes Y and Z.

clue.text: Native guides in no distress

indicators.note: distress as a verb here means to damage or rough up, so these letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Local people guide visitors without any hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distress' rearranges GUIDES IN NO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigenous peoples are those native to a place, original inhabitants.

clue.text: Daniel, pickpocket and renegade, was long ago a whippersnapper

parts.note: dip is slang for a pickpocket
a rat is a deserter or traitor

explanation.surface: A man of shady character was in his youth a cheeky young upstart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was long ago a' tells us the word is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandiprat is an old word for an insignificant, presumptuous little fellow.

clue.text: Objection's reversed by the counterfoil

indicators.note: reversed tells us the word for objections is read from end to start

parts.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: A protest overturned by producing the receipt counterfoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns BUTS around to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a cheque or ticket kept as a record is its stub.

clue.text: Bird ended in poor shape unable to get up

indicators.note: in poor shape suggests these letters are mangled out of their order

explanation.surface: A bird finished up in such bad condition it could not rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in poor shape' rearranges BIRD ENDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bedridden is confined to bed, too ill to rise.

clue.text: Utter a rival's name

definitions.meaning: Captain ... is a character in Sheridan's comedy The Rivals

explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means total or complete; Jack Absolute is a suitor in Sheridan's play The Rivals.

clue.text: Swim, or here you will get washed up

definitions.text: here you will get washed up
definitions.meaning: a kitchen basin where dishes are washed up

explanation.surface: A dare: swim for it, or you will end up stranded on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washed up' suggests a shipwreck, but it is the dishes being cleaned.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'sink or swim' supplies one sense; the other is the basin where washing-up is done.

clue.text: "Nymph, in thy orisons Be all my sins ——" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: "Nymph, in thy orisons Be all my sins ——" (Hamlet)

parts.words: "Nymph, in thy orisons Be all my sins ——" (Hamlet)
parts.note: the missing last word of Hamlet's line to Ophelia, asking her to recall his sins in her prayers

explanation.surface: Hamlet asks Ophelia to pray for him, with the final word left blank.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line ends with the word meaning recalled in memory, here in her prayers.

clue.text: Pope was English and a right one for trouble

indicators.note: for trouble means these letters are stirred up and disturbed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An English pope was a fair candidate for causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was English' adds detail: Adrian IV was the only English pope. 'for trouble' rearranges AND A R I.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrian is the name taken by several pontiffs, including Nicholas Breakspear, Adrian IV.

clue.text: Your worship's desk, French style

parts.note: a kneeling desk for prayer whose French name means pray to God

explanation.surface: A magistrate's bench designed with French flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your worship' is the address for a magistrate, but here worship means prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A prie-dieu is a kneeling desk used for private prayer, named from the French for pray God.

clue.text: Did some road-work, not without flagging

definitions.meaning: laid a hard surface on a road
laid with flagstones, so having flagging

explanation.surface: Someone surfaced a road and kept going despite tiring.
explanation.definitionFit: To surface a street is to pave it, and flagstones form a paved path.

clue.text: African Prophet — backed £1

indicators.note: backed means the prophet's name is run backwards

parts.note: Amos is an Old Testament prophet
L is the pound sign's letter and I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An African prophet given financial support of one pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns AMOS into SOMA; then £1 gives L (pound) and I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: A Somali is a native of Somalia in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Range of great extent and sound comfort

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for comfort is spoken, giving letters that match its pronunciation

parts.note: ease is comfort or relaxation

explanation.surface: A vast mountain chain that also offers solid relaxation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'solid' but means said aloud: AND + 'ease' said aloud gives the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes is the long South American mountain chain, the world's longest.

clue.text: How his Grace signs for the vestment sent up

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a robe is a ceremonial garment, a vestment

explanation.surface: A bishop signs for a robe sent upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archbishop of York, addressed as his Grace, signs with the Latin abbreviation Ebor (Eboracum, York).
explanation.definitionFit: The Archbishop of York signs his name with the Latin form of his see.

clue.text: He produced music from a silver dish

indicators.note: from shows the composer is taken out of the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A musician who conjures tunes out of a silver plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was an Italian opera composer.

clue.text: Describes scope of editor no longer tied

parts.note: unbound means freed from ties

explanation.surface: An editor freed from restraint describes the range of his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; the word for editor comes after the word for no longer tied.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlimited range or scope is called unbounded, as in boundless possibility.

clue.text: It could make a rotten do go with a bang

definitions.text: It could make a rotten do go with a bang

indicators.note: could make signals these letters can be made into something else by rearranging

explanation.surface: Something that would liven up a dull party with an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges A ROTTEN DO; the whole clue also describes the device.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is the device that sets off an explosive charge.

clue.text: Two quarters we hear of in a German town?

indicators.note: we hear tells us the letters are spoken aloud as their names

parts.note: S and N are compass points, quarters of the compass, south and north

explanation.surface: Two districts said to be found in a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: The two compass letters S and N, said aloud, sound like 'ess-en'. 'quarters' looks like town districts.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr, western Germany.
